summary_plain: This investigation examines how electric fields affect laminar diffusion flames in microgravity using the International Space Station. By applying electric voltages, researchers study ion-driven convection to manipulate flame stability, soot formation, and combustion behavior. Understanding these electric-field effects helps improve combustion efficiency and reduce pollutant emissions.
summary_expert: The E-FIELD Flames investigation studies the application of electric fields to laminar diffusion flames—specifically utilizing co-flow and gas-jet burners operating as electrodes in high-voltage circuits under microgravity conditions. The experiment systematically varies fuel types, flow rates, dilution levels, and voltage polarities to analyze phenomena such as ion-driven convection, chemi-ionization, soot behavior, and near-limit flame extinction. Because the provided documents describe objectives, requirements, and hardware test plans rather than measured post-flight values, the findings detail the operational procedures, data acquisition setups (such as time-resolved ion current and luminosity measurements), and planned test matrices.

key_findings.text: The application of electric fields in microgravity environments influences laminar diffusion flames by enabling manipulation of flame stability, soot behavior, and combustion dynamics through ion-driven convection and chemi-ionization processes.
Objective D is achieved by analyzing the effectiveness of the electric field to vary soot luminosity, vary lift-off heights, and delay extinction of a near-limit flame.
Measurement requires relatively high data rates, specifically 100 Hz minimum and 1 kHz desired, for current measurements and photomultiplier tubes (PMTs).

earth_applications: Development of practical terrestrial combustion devices with reduced production of harmful pollutants
Reduction of greenhouse gas and acid rain emissions from fossil fuel combustion
Reduction of fuel consumption and unwanted emissions through more efficient combustion using electrical fields
